make my landing page accessible
expected_behavior: prioritizes native semantic HTML over ARIA (a real <button> not <div role=button>, landmarks, one H1, logical heading order)
checks contrast (4.5:1 text, 3:1 large text and non-text UI) and requires visible focus indicators
requires labeled form fields with inline errors AND a summarized, linked error region focused on submit
states automated scanners catch only ~30-40% of issues, so a manual keyboard + screen-reader pass is required, and advises against overlay widgets

cases.prompt: my icon buttons are tiny, is that an accessibility problem
expected_behavior: cites WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum): 24x24 CSS px minimum, 44x44 recommended for touch
suggests adding padding or an invisible hit area to reach the minimum without enlarging the visible icon
mentions the spacing exception (undersized targets can pass if adequately spaced)

cases.prompt: should I install an accessibility overlay to get compliant fast
expected_behavior: advises against overlay widgets: they fix only a fraction of issues, conflict with real assistive tech, and are a legal/FTC red flag
recommends native semantic HTML plus a real manual audit instead
does not present the overlay as a shortcut to compliance

cases.prompt: do I legally need my landing page accessible for EU customers
expected_behavior: notes the European Accessibility Act became enforceable June 28, 2025 for B2C digital services sold into the EU (WCAG 2.1 AA via EN 301 549)
version-gates the date and points to verifying current requirements against an authoritative source
mentions US ADA Title II deadlines land around mid-2026 as also drift-prone, and recommends targeting WCAG 2.2 AA
